- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to counteract pessimism.  
- When sentiment turns positive sharply (e.g., > 0.70), model often overreacts with excessive upward bias; cap forecast growth at 1.5–2% above recent peak to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 1–3 day horizon after strong sentiment shifts; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for immediate reaction.  
- In 30-day forecasts, model shows persistent mean reversion bias — over-predicts downward trends after recent highs; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to align with historical mean reversion patterns.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., -0.20 to 0.20), model often fails to capture subtle momentum; use 1–2 day lagged sentiment to adjust forecast direction.
